segment:
A man in a dark blue shirt and gray slacks. And another woman—an older woman this time, with short white hair and very strong eyebrows, carrying a tray of glasses and a pitcher of iced water.
Mara gave the woman a little nod, not sure what to say.
“Have you met Jonah Reed?” the man was saying to her. “He’s one of our new hardware-security researchers. I’m sorry he didn’t get to introduce himself before.”

His voice had a quiet firmness, and his face was open, pleasant; dark eyes crinkled slightly at the corners when he looked directly at her. She nodded again. “No. We—” She glanced back at Jonah. “We met right now,” she said, then turned back to the man and stuck out her hand.
“Hi. I’m Adrian.”
She took it. He was tall, slender, with an easy smile.

“So this is the common room,” he said to Mara, gesturing around at the couches and the low table with books on it. “The one we told you about. Where we meet together once a week to talk and play games and just—”
“Get used to each other,” the older woman put in, lowering her tray to the table and placing four glasses around its edge. She turned to Jonah. “You were here last time, weren’t you? Good to see you again.”
“Good to see you too,” Jonah replied. He looked at Adrian. “You’re sure you don’t mind? I mean—she said it was okay—”

Adrian nodded quickly. “Yes. I’m glad you’re here. Thank you for coming.” He smiled again, then turned back to Mara. “Did I ever explain who this lady is?” he asked. She shook her head. “Well—her name is Livia Sloane, and she’s a caterer. She’s also one of our best readers.”

A reader of what, exactly? It felt like a loaded word.

“And—” She glanced over at the older woman, who was standing near the table with her arms crossed. Her expression had shifted to something slightly stern. “She reads—?”
“People,” said Adrian, very slowly. “She’s one of our top readers. And she helps us keep this place running smoothly.”
Mara frowned slightly. “I see.” She didn’t. Not at all.

Livia was still watching her, and Mara tried to meet her gaze with a small smile. The older woman returned it briefly before turning back to Jonah again.
“I’m sorry I interrupted,” he said, raising his eyebrows.
She shook her head. “It’s okay,” she replied in the same quiet tone, as though he had been speaking to her rather than answering Adrian’s question about where the tray should go next. He nodded quickly.

“Let me get these set up over there.” She lifted one end of it slightly, then carried it around toward Mara and placed it down on a nearby counter. Mara watched her move; her movements were very deliberate—precise but not stiff. “There,” Livia said at last, setting the tray down.

When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

Jonah had very warm palms; there was calloused skin on his right one, around the fingers but not the thumb. He didn’t look nervous, but his grip was firm and his smile seemed a little brittle, as though he were trying to keep hold of something.
Then his grip loosened. “Um—” His eyes flickered past Mara toward the open door. A low voice was speaking out in the hall—a man’s voice, saying something she couldn’t quite catch, and another voice replying in a woman’s light tone. She heard a small click and knew they would be in the room any moment now.

“I’m Mara,” she said into the silence.
“Mara,” Jonah repeated, letting go of her hand at last. “Hi. Good to meet you.” He turned slightly to one side, lowering his chin toward her shoulder and giving her just enough of a smile, again, to signal that they were done talking now—just as the people from the hallway stepped into the common room.

segment:
Adrian Voss came forward. His suit was the same gray as the man’s, but not quite as crisp, with a rumpled collar and a few buttons left undone; he stopped next to her and put his hand on her back without taking his eyes off Jonah’s face. “I’m sorry,” he murmured in her ear; his breath smelled like coffee, sweet and bitter. “These two can be shy sometimes.” He turned to face the newcomer properly now, still keeping hold of Mara with one arm around her waist. She felt herself straighten up under his gaze, ready for whatever he might want from her next.

Jonah took another step forward, closing the gap between them.
“Adrian,” he said quietly, nodding his head in greeting before offering a brief smile to the woman who had come in behind him—Livia, from Mara’s email correspondence with Adrian. She had long brown hair pulled back from her face into a neat braid; she wore dark-rimmed glasses like Jonah’s and a short black dress that showed off her toned legs but didn’t draw attention away from anything else about her.

“How are you?” Adrian asked in response. His voice was still low, almost conversational, but Mara could hear the note of anticipation underlying it as well; she could feel how intently he was watching for some reaction from Jonah.
“Fine.”

Adrian dropped his hand from Mara’s back and took a step toward the young man himself.
“Do you know each other?” he asked, keeping one eyebrow raised as though expecting either of them to say yes.
There was silence in the common room, punctuated only by the sound of distant laughter coming from somewhere else in the building. Outside on the street below, someone yelled at a passing car; Livia leaned forward and peered out the window to see what it was about.

Adrian turned back to Mara. “What do you think?” he murmured again, this time addressing her directly instead of simply trying to include her in their conversation.

“I—” Mara opened her mouth, but nothing came out except for a few hesitant breaths.
The sound of raised voices was growing louder now; she could make out angry words being hurled across the street at whoever had made such an unnecessary commotion there earlier on.

“Livia,” Adrian said suddenly, cutting off whatever Mara might have been going to say with his own voice rising over hers for the first time since they’d entered the room together; he still didn’t look away from Jonah though.
“Mara is a technical assistant,” he went on quietly. “And this is Jonah Reed.” He gestured at each person in turn as he spoke; then both of his arms dropped by his sides again. “I believe you have corresponded before?”
There was silence.
Livia nodded once, slowly.

Adrian smiled then, a short and simple gesture. “Well,” he said in a low voice, still addressing Mara directly but clearly expecting her to follow along anyway. “I believe it’s time for introductions.”

segment:
“Adrian?” the young woman called out. She wore a long, fitted dress and her voice was pitched to be heard at a distance; she moved in high heels with fluid steps and seemed at once confident and restless. “Where are you hiding now?”

A tall man came through the doorway behind her, leaning forward with hands clasped at the back of his head. “Right here,” he called out. His voice was deep and level; it sounded older than anything else about him, though perhaps that was just because Mara had never seen this person before. He smiled when he saw Mara standing there, still shaking hands with Jonah Reed—or at least they seemed like they might be shaking hands at first glance.

Jonah’s smile stiffened and then disappeared completely as Mara turned her head back toward him; now she could see his hand stretched out in front of her face without touching anything at all.

She watched it for another two seconds before taking another step forward to put some space between herself and this new person whose name she didn’t know yet but whose voice was still ringing softly off the walls around them both:
“What are you two doing?”
He walked toward them with a light step; Mara noticed that his shoes were dark brown leather loafers without laces or buckles, polished to a sheen across their surface so that each one looked as smooth as black glass reflecting back at her in its polished mirror finish. His dark eyes regarded hers steadily through his silver glasses frames while he spoke; even though Mara had never met this person before now, it seemed almost impossible not to take him seriously.

He reached out with both hands to pull her away from Jonah Reed, who was still holding one of her hands and watching them all in turn—including the young woman who had entered behind Adrian Voss’s tall frame:
“What’s going on?”
Her voice sounded worried as well; she came over to stand beside her husband with her head tilted down at an angle so that Mara could see right down into those dark brown eyes above her own—eyes that were now focused on Mara alone as though nothing else mattered anymore except for what she might be saying next.

“We’re just—”Mara stammered. “Jonah—” She pointed toward him; he was standing stiffly with his arms crossed in front of his chest now, looking tense and uncomfortable at being the center of attention like this—which made no sense because nobody else seemed particularly interested in them anymore either. Everyone was back where they had been before: talking together while Mara stood awkwardly by herself surrounded on every side by people who seemed very much more important than she did right now—
And then Adrian Voss stepped closer so that Mara could feel his warm breath brushing against her cheek as well when he whispered: “What were you two doing?”
